title: PQC Protocol Readiness Matrix entry
description: One protocol-and-mechanism-class pair's post-quantum readiness, recorded so every claim carries its own provenance. Strawman for OWASP/quantum-security-project#46. Version 2: rebuilt after an adversarial review in which 5 of 6 deliberately false rows passed version 1.

schema_version.description: Pinned so an enum can be split later without a flag day. A version 1 file is rejected rather than migrated; there is no previous-major support and any change is a flag day today.

slug.description: Must equal the filename stem. The validator enforces that and global uniqueness, so two contradictory rows for one protocol cannot both pass.

mechanism_class.description: The axis a defender actually asks about, and the single most misleading omission in version 1. TLS 1.3 key establishment is published and on by default; TLS authentication with PQ certificates is not. One row cannot answer both, so a protocol gets one row per class.

maintainer.description: A real GitHub handle, validated by shape. Required, because an unowned row is the one that goes stale.

row_state.description: An orphaned row is visible rather than fatal. A stale needs-owner row raises an issue; it does not fail the build forever.

status.description: superseded means replaced by something better. deprecated and withdrawn are separate values because they imply the opposite deployment decision and version 1 conflated all three.

documents.description: Empty only when status is 'none', 'draft' or 'wg-draft'; the conditional below requires at least one document for 'approved' and later. A status with no document is not a claim, and this is a constraint rather than a comment.

version.description: The version in which it became true. 'latest' is rejected by pattern, not by prose.

withdrawn_in_version.description: Set when support was removed. Recording a revert must not require deleting history, which was the only option in version 1.

status.description: Outcome, not ceremony. Version 1 let a multi-vendor plugfest at which everything failed outrank a successful pairwise test, so 'plugfest' is gone and the validator requires at least one interoperating pair.

Carries readiness signal. Version 1's not_assessed/assessed rendered a protocol that aborts safely and one that silently reverts to classical identically, in the axis the proposal calls most important.

class.description: Structured, because the proposal's whole complaint about PQUIP is evidence in a free-text column nothing validates, and version 1 put the exposures in free text.

evidence.description: Optional, and the gate reports each exposure that omits it. Version 2 set additionalProperties: false here with no evidence property at all, so the five exposures on the exemplar had nowhere to put any.

related_owasp_entries.description: Validated against a committed top10 manifest rather than by regex alone, so a renumber does not silently break every row.

notes.description: Capped so substance cannot migrate out of the structured fields into prose.

date.description: Pattern rejects 2026-13-45. It still admits 2026-02-30, which the validator catches by actually parsing the date; version 1 crashed on exactly that input and silently skipped every later row.

status.description: Proposed Standard IS standards-track, so version 1 offering both guaranteed two contributors would tag the same RFC differently. 'standards-track' is removed.

superseded_by.description: When set, the axis status must be superseded, deprecated or withdrawn. This is what rule 3 in version 1 was reaching for and could not express: it checked that a draft name looked versioned, which cannot see a rename.

source_kind.description: Split from independence, because version 1's single anchor enum made release-notes and vendor-statement overlap: release notes ARE a vendor statement.

independence.description: The relation between the evidence's AUTHOR and the SUBJECT of the claim, and nothing else. Reproducibility is a separate field, because it is a property of method rather than of authorship. Apply the tests in order and take the first that matches: first-party, the author and the subject share an interest; derivative, the author is not the subject but the content restates the subject's own assertion rather than independently establishing it; third-party, the author is not the subject and did not take the subject's word for it; unknown, authorship or affiliation cannot be established from the source. The order is the precedence rule: version 1 had none, so a vendor's own pinned harness had two defensible values. Independence is a property of the evidence-to-claim PAIR, not of the document, so the same URL can carry different values on different rows. Worked cases in README.md.
independence.$comment: Reworked after the second round of review on issue #46. `unknown` was added in the first round because the enum could not say 'not established' while the field was required. `independently-reproducible` was REMOVED in this round and `derivative` added: the first conflated method with authorship, and without the second the authorship axis was not exhaustive.

independence_basis.description: Required on every value: one sentence naming who authored the evidence and how that relates to the subject of this claim. For `unknown`, why it could not be established.
independence_basis.$comment: Required on all four values after the second round of review on issue #46. The first round required it only on `unknown` and `independently-reproducible`, on the argument that the other two were cheap to check against the source URL. The argument was wrong on this repo's own evidence: the exemplar labelled RFC 10024 `third-party` for the claim that RFC 10024 is published, and a URL shows a host, not an authorship. Requiring the sentence is what surfaces the mislabel.

reproduction.description: Optional. What a reader would re-run, against which pinned artifacts, to reach the same answer. Split out of the independence enum, where it was the value `independently-reproducible`.
reproduction.$comment: This field earns a row nothing. Nothing in validate.py re-runs anything, so the field is an instruction to a human reader and the gate treats it as census data. It is deliberately not a grade: in the first round the strongest-sounding enum value was the better-rewarded lie, because a fabricated row recovered a pass for one character of basis text and then printed as the most independent row in the repo. See gap 3 in README.md for the check that would make it mean something.

source.$comment: The gate additionally REJECTS a source whose host cannot carry a real citation: the documentation and non-resolvable names in the IANA Special-Use Domain Names registry (RFC 6761, which updates RFC 2606) plus ICANN's .internal, and any IP literal that is not globally reachable, which covers RFC 5737 and RFC 3849 documentation ranges as well as loopback, link-local and RFC 1918. That check is in validate.py rather than here, because expressing it as a pattern needs a negative lookahead that no reviewer can audit by eye, and because the IP test belongs in code; the cost is that a consumer validating against this schema alone does not get it.

verbatim.description: Required with an excerpt. `yes` means the excerpt is a quotation of the source's TEXT with whitespace normalised. It does NOT mean the excerpt is a byte substring of what the URL serves. Version 1 called the field 'quote' and its own exemplar put an editorial paraphrase in it.
verbatim.$comment: Defined on 2026-10-31 because it was undefined, then sharpened the same day because the first definition said 'whitespace normalised' and that was still not true of all nine excerpts on the exemplar. Measured: three are byte-identical to the source, three more match after whitespace normalisation of a hard-wrapped file, and three need the markup stripped first, because the sentence a reader quotes from an HTML page or a POD file is split across tags. All nine are quotations of their source's text; none of the last six is a byte substring. This is exactly why gap 3 is not closed by a one-line check: the extraction step is source-type dependent, so an excerpt checker needs a text extractor per source kind before it can compare anything, and a naive tag-strip regex eats OpenSSL's POD markup `C<?>` and reports a false mismatch.

verification.description: An INDEPENDENT verification of this evidence, attributed to whoever performed it. Optional, and never inferred from an `independence` value: a `third-party` label says who wrote the source, not that anybody checked it. Raised by @leprecha1 on issue #46.

verified_by.description: Who verified it, as a name, handle or organisation. Required, because an unattributed attestation is the thing this field exists to replace. The row's own maintainer may appear here, and that is not independent verification: it is a self-attestation and a reader can see whose name it carries.

method.description: What they did, specifically enough for a third person to repeat.

source.description: Optional link to the attestation itself.

verification.$comment: Distinct from `reproduction`, which names what a reader COULD re-run. This field records that somebody DID, and who. The gate reads neither: it counts them and changes no verdict, because nothing offline can check either claim.

disputed.description: A recorded disagreement with this evidence, pointing at an issue or discussion. Optional. This is gap 5's mechanism, proposed by @leprecha1 on issue #46 as a lightweight alternative to an adjudication workflow: the disagreement becomes part of the row, travels with it, and is printed by the gate.

url.description: The issue, PR or discussion where the disagreement is argued.

note.description: What is disputed, in one sentence.

disputed.$comment: Deliberately not a status. The gate does not decide who is right, and a disputed row still passes; the point is that a reader who disagrees has somewhere in the DATA to say so, which printing provenance never gave them. It also cannot be gamed: adding a dispute makes a row noisier, so nothing rewards a false one.
